memos.headline: Momentum leaders S07/S09/S05 dominate while S04 and S08 flash oversold signals in a bifurcated tape
memos.body: I see a sharply divided market as of January 16. The strongest relative-strength names—S07 (+59.4% over 26w, RSI 68.3, sitting at its 52w high), S05 (+81.8% over 26w, RSI 64.0, just 1.8% off highs), and S09 (+14.0% over 26w, RSI 67.1, essentially at highs)—continue to trend well above both their 50d and 200d means and are outperforming SPY on every timeframe. On the other side, S04 is deeply oversold with an RSI of 33.8, trading 5.2% below its 50d and 4.6% below its 200d, down 15.2% from its 52w high, and underperforming SPY by 14.2% over 12 weeks—a clear downtrend I want to avoid until price reclaims the 200d. S08 has the lowest RSI in the universe at 25.2 and is 5.9% below its 50d, which could set up a mean-reversion bounce, but the negative relative strength (-9.0% vs SPY over 4w) keeps me cautious. I am most convicted on riding the S07 and S09 trends while steering clear of S04's persistent weakness; a close below 120 on S09 or below 580 on S07 would change my view.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Best Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Face Margin Compression
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between durable high-margin growers and names suffering earnings deterioration. S10 stands out with 56% net margins, +62.5% YoY revenue growth, and minimal debt ($8.5B), making it the strongest fundamental profile in the group. S05 delivers 34.2% net margins on $102B revenue with +33% net income growth and a clean balance sheet ($14.8B debt). On the other end, S02 posted a 2.1% net margin with net income collapsing -61.2% YoY despite +12.2% revenue growth—classic cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for. S09 is the only name with negative revenue growth (-5.2%) and shrinking earnings (-12.3%), and its 8.8% margin leaves little cushion. I would need to see margin stabilization in S02 and a return to top-line growth in S09 before reconsidering either.

views.note: 56% net margin, +62.5% revenue growth, near-zero leverage at $8.5B debt—best earnings quality in the universe.

35.7% net margin and +18.4% revenue growth are strong, though +12.5% net income growth lags revenue, suggesting some cost pressure worth monitoring.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Pausing as Sticky Inflation and Rising Long Rates Complicate the Outlook
memos.body: I see the Fed in a late-easing / early-pause regime. The upper bound has come down 75bp over the past year to 3.75%, but CPI is running at +2.7% y/y with a 3-month pace of +0.6% (roughly 2.4% annualized), suggesting disinflation has stalled. Unemployment at 4.40% is flat over three months but up 30bp y/y, indicating a labor market that is softening only gradually—not enough to force further cuts. The 10y yield at 4.24% has risen 25bp over three months even as the front end eased, steepening the 10y-2y spread to +61bp; this bear-steepening signals the market is repricing term premium and inflation risk higher. A renewed acceleration in CPI above 3% or a jump in unemployment above 4.6% would change my regime call; absent that, I expect the Fed to hold and long rates to stay elevated, favoring banks and staples over duration-sensitive growth and pure cyclicals.

views.note: Banks benefit from a positively sloped curve (10y-2y at +61bp, up 22bp y/y) and a pause that keeps net interest margins healthy.
Staples offer defensive positioning in a late-cycle pause with sticky inflation and limited further easing expected.
Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds from the 25bp rise in 10y yields over three months and a Fed unlikely to cut further near-term.
Cyclicals are caught between a still-employed consumer and rising long rates; I lack conviction either way until labor data clarifies.
Energy is macro-neutral here—inflation is sticky but not accelerating, and the growth outlook is ambiguous.
High-duration tech/growth names face valuation pressure as the 10y yield grinds higher and the easing cycle stalls.

memos.headline: S06 Negative Tone Shift on Earnings Miss Stands Out; Rest of Universe Dominated by Routine Officer Turnover Noise
memos.body: I see one clear sentiment signal in this universe: S06 dropped 4.2% on its Jan 13 results-of-operations 8-K, accompanied by a same-day Reg FD disclosure, suggesting disappointing preliminary numbers and a genuine negative narrative shift. Across the rest of the universe, the dominant filing type is Departure/Appointment of Directors or Officers, which I treat as low-signal noise absent additional context—S08 had two such filings in five weeks, but without tone data beyond the filing headers I cannot distinguish routine succession from destabilizing turnover. S01, S02, and S09 each paired a late-2025 officer change with a January Reg FD disclosure, likely investor-day or conference presentations; these are neutral-to-mildly-positive information events that rarely shift sentiment durably. I have highest conviction on avoiding S06 near-term given the fresh negative price reaction, and I remain neutral elsewhere due to insufficient tone differentiation.

views.note: Fresh -4.2% price reaction to Jan 13 earnings 8-K signals a genuine negative tone shift that may not yet be fully priced.
Two officer-change 8-Ks in five weeks could flag instability but without broader tone data this is noise.
Officer change plus a Reg FD disclosure suggest routine investor communication, no clear sentiment direction.
Nov officer departure followed by Jan Reg FD disclosure is standard cadence with no discernible tone shift.
Officer change and subsequent Reg FD filing appear routine; insufficient evidence of a narrative shift.
Bylaws amendment alongside officer changes is unusual but without price or tone data I cannot form a directional view.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Surges 156% in Three Months While Credit Markets Shrug — Divergence Signals Latent Geopolitical Risk
memos.body: I am flagging a stark divergence: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has spiked to 410, up 61% in one month and 156% over three months, yet VIX sits at a benign 15.84 (down 23% over three months) and HY OAS has actually tightened 24bp over the same period. This pattern — elevated policy noise with complacent risk pricing — historically precedes abrupt repricing when a concrete policy action (sanctions escalation, export-control expansion, energy embargo) crystallizes. WTI at $59.13 is essentially flat over three months, suggesting energy supply-chain disruption is not yet priced, but the policy uncertainty spike could reflect brewing trade or technology-control actions. Several names in the universe filed Reg FD 8-Ks in early January (S06, S01, S02, S09), which may relate to forward guidance adjustments amid the uncertain policy backdrop, though the filings lack detail on specific geopolitical exposures. I have moderate conviction that names with high China/export-control exposure or energy-supply-chain concentration face asymmetric downside if the policy uncertainty translates into concrete action, and I would favor domestically oriented or defensively positioned names until the divergence resolves.

views.note: Recent Reg FD filing may signal management positioning ahead of policy shifts, but without detail on geopolitical exposure I stay neutral pending clarity.
Reg FD disclosure on Jan 13 coincides with the policy-uncertainty spike; I need more information on supply-chain concentration before taking a directional view.
Filed Reg FD on Jan 12; the benign credit spread environment (HY OAS 2.71%) provides a cushion, but the policy uncertainty overhang warrants caution.

Earliest Reg FD filer (Jan 7) in the universe during the uncertainty ramp; if this name has meaningful export or China exposure, the 156% policy-uncertainty surge argues for caution until concrete policy actions are clarified.
No adverse 8-K filings and stable energy prices at $59 suggest domestically oriented names without geopolitical overhang may benefit from the VIX compression and tight credit spreads.
No company-specific evidence available; the macro divergence between policy uncertainty and market volatility keeps me sidelined until the picture clarifies.
